method: Measured at commit `1388f2cc6` (origin/main, 29 Sep 2026 08:24 UTC, after #1332) in a separate read-only worktree, 84 commits and 1,165 changed files after the second scoring at `0c8225d58`. Nothing in the repository was changed.

The lead ran typecheck, lint, Prettier, knip, the dist drift check and the full node suite, re-ran the 26 September metric script for like-for-like numbers, and re-read the register and the branch protection. Eleven reviewers each took two to five categories, marked every bullet of the category's checklist as holds, partly, absent or not applicable with a citation, re-verified every 28 September claim against the code, named the pull request behind each change, re-scored with the same rubric, re-checked all 64 known defects, and read the code merged since for new ones. The lead then re-ran or re-read every new medium: the broadcast that fails its list when Graph is unreachable (run), the review sweep on a paused workspace (read), the message insert policy that names no parent tenant (read), the settings rollback regression (run), and the Ask microphone claim (read, and lowered to low: the recogniser is stopped; only its last words are asked).

Rubric, unchanged: **10** means nothing material is left: the practice is universal, a test or tool stops it regressing, it is documented, and it fits Chanlytics' scale. **8–9** is strong with bounded gaps. **6–7** means the pattern exists but has notable exceptions or no enforcement. **4–5** is inconsistent. **2–3** is mostly absent. A number a ratchet holds is enforcement; a number that merely fell is not. The overall figure is the plain mean of the 40.

Duplicates across reviewers were folded: the broadcast defect (found by two), the copied CSV rules (two), the partner-role nightly test (two) and the register's missing falls-when cells (two) each appear once.

moves.why: The three high and the worst medium findings are small, contained fixes: the strict config read that can silence the receptionist, core refusals shown as 500, erasure leaving numbers in job rows, cross-tenant media, the playbooks sweep's 25-playbook ceiling, the reply idempotency race, the missing money rule and the dollar-only price check. Most are a day each.

moves.now: Of the eight named: the sweep ceiling, cross-tenant media and the erasure digest closed this round; the reply race, the 500s, the config read and the erasure scrub stayed closed. Open: the money rule and the price check.

moves.t: Turn every drift you already measure into a ratchet
moves.why: Ratchets work here: text assertions fell from 914 to 873, and undeclared routes reached 0. Everything without one grew. One PR can add may-only-fall baselines for function length and branching, lint warnings, `as unknown as`, `window.__` names, `.from(` outside `packages/db`, dead exports and flat-directory size.
moves.lifts: Complexity, code smells, static analysis, organization, architecture, maintainability, debt
moves.now: Sixteen baselines now, every bank taking only falls. Still outside a ratchet: `.rpc(` calls (129, rising), `as never` (39), the packages' own unread exports, duplicate bodies.

moves.t: Make the tests see what production sees
moves.why: Three blind spots have each already let a bug through. The fake database has no triggers (#1100). No test runs a route through `withRoute` on the built dists (the 500s). The forward-compatibility test checks only the top level of the config (the silent receptionist). Fixes: generate the fake's constraints from the schema, run core verbs through `withRoute`, add core, jobs, the edge and the server to the database-suite paths, and pin the time zone.
moves.now: Two tests run through the real `withRoute` on the built dists. The fake database still has no triggers or CHECKs, `DB_PATHS` is unchanged, and the time zone is not pinned.

moves.t: Type-aware lint and one more strict flag
moves.why: Turn on typescript-eslint's type-aware rules (`no-floating-promises`, `switch-exhaustiveness-check`, `no-unnecessary-type-assertion`) and `--max-warnings 0`. Fix the shell's hooks alias list, which leaves 82 effects unchecked. Enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on the edge (9 errors) and in core (39).
moves.lifts: Static analysis, type system, async, frontend
moves.now: One compiler, type tests, unused names and hook aliases as errors. No type-aware rule runs and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off everywhere.

moves.why: Core's build inlines contracts: 1.7 MB of dist for 7.9k source lines. That is why errors lose their class, why a contracts change rebuilds five bundles, and why 21 of the last 60 commits rewrite dist. Either externalise `@chanlytics/*` in each package's build and handle Vercel's symlink limit once, at the edge's import shim, or keep bundling and give every shared class a structural brand.
moves.now: The error brand only. All four builds inline `@chanlytics/*`; core's dist is 1.88 MB; no packaging note or date.

moves.t: One request id, one logger, and somewhere to send them
moves.why: Mint a request id in `withRoute`, sign it into the edge token and carry it in job payloads. Move `log.ts` into a package so the dashboard and the packages log the way the edge does. Add a log drain, an external pinger with SMS or push on `/api/health`, and a client error beacon.
moves.lifts: Observability, error handling, data flow, events
moves.now: A request id from `withRoute` to the edge's admin doors, and one dashboard logger. Jobs, webhooks and events carry no id; the logger is a second copy, not a package; no drain, pinger or error beacon.

moves.t: One provider fetch with typed outcomes
moves.why: Add a `providerFetch` in `channels` with a mandatory timeout, returning a `SendOutcome` (sent, refused, throttled, unavailable, auth, unknown) mapped from Meta and Twilio codes. Retries and circuit breakers then key on the outcome, and a 429 stops a broadcast instead of failing every remaining recipient.
moves.now: `providerFetch`: a required timeout, four outcomes, retry by outcome, a breaker per provider; 16 unbounded server fetches are 0. Left: provider codes past the throttle still read “HTTP n”, and a broadcast ignores a `retryable` connection (a new defect below).

moves.t: Give the job ledger lanes and fairness
moves.why: Today an Inbox reply waits behind a 2,000-person broadcast. Give replies their own lane first, round-robin between workspaces, and run a few claims in parallel per tick. Add a purge clock and a tenant index, defer unknown job kinds instead of failing them, and make the playbook and calendar sweeps due-aware.
moves.now: The purge clock, due-aware sweeps and a per-kind lateness measure landed. Lanes, fairness, jitter, a tenant index and deferred unknown kinds are not built: a reply can still wait behind a broadcast.

moves.t: Close the rollout fallbacks and add a second factor
moves.why: Refuse `DIAG_KEY` on admin doors and make the voice doors signature-only. Bind every edge token to a workspace and a person, with a nonce. Require MFA for owners and platform admins. Add CSP nonces, SAST and an audit gate in CI, and a dashboard env module whose security switches fail closed.
moves.now: The partner definer doors are gated (00261, one left out). `DIAG_KEY` still opens preview doors, the voice switch defaults on, owners and admins have no second factor, no nonce check, no CSP nonces, no SAST.

moves.t: One model layer and a nightly eval
moves.why: A model registry by purpose (model, fallback, timeout, cap) that records tokens and dollars on every call and stamps the prompt hash on every output. A nightly eval on a sandbox key with pass thresholds and cases for injection, money and currencies. One prompt-injection policy for every agent.
moves.lifts: AI architecture, AI safety, product, observability
moves.now: Ask's answers carry a prompt hash and the nightly checks Ask's day. Still no model registry by purpose, no fallback model, no dollars, evals by hand on the production key.

moves.t: Make what happens after merge safe
moves.why: Stop cancelling main runs, and add a merge queue and `enforce_admins`. Alarm when production lacks a migration that main has. Use a Supabase branch as staging for previews, the nightly and e2e, so no test writes to production.

cats.name: Architecture & System Design
cats.verdict: The shape is better held than on 28 September. The receptionist's path now follows decision 0001's layout, channels are grouped by provider, tooling by job, and every tree follows the second-module rule under a test. The docs' tree and paths are tested, four decisions are accepted, and one providerFetch is the way out to seven providers. But the three small steps named on both 26 and 28 September have not moved. The core wall still scans 46 of core's 75 files, core and jobs still import a package they do not declare, and `.rpc(` is still uncounted (120 to 129). Meanwhile SQL grew from 259 to 302 functions with no note on when a rule belongs in SQL.
evidence: **Fitness functions multiplied and all pass at `1388f2cc6`.** There are 16 may-only-fall baselines, and the lint and bundle banks now take only falls (#1257, `tooling/scripts/checks/lint.mjs:59`). `docs-tree.test.mjs` redraws `docs/architecture.md:318-458` from the tree, and `docs-paths.test.mjs` (5 tests) opens every path the maps name. `contracts-barrels.test.mjs:342` fails any folder with one module in every tree (#1286), with one dated exception (`:288`). `history/decisions.test.mjs` (4 tests) holds the decisions index.

**The layers hold by lint and resolution.** `lint-boundaries.test.mjs` passes 19 tests over `BROWSER_/SERVER_/EDGE_MAY_NOT_IMPORT` (`eslint.config.mjs:104,125,144`), and `.npmrc:5` injects workspace packages. My scan (`review3/A/declared-deps.mjs`) finds contracts importing zod alone, db and channels importing contracts, and the only contracts cycle as the allowed signup↔workspace (`contracts-import-cycles.test.mjs`).

**The inbound verb follows 0001's layout (#1268).** `answerInbound` is 18 lines at cyclomatic 8 (`packages/core/src/inbound/answer.ts:78`), down from 920 lines at 139, over phase modules that share one `Answering` record (`context.ts:110`). The largest phase is `firstGates`, 126 lines (`gates.ts:42`).

**The core wall has not changed.** `repo/hygiene.test.mjs:209` scans four folders. Run over all of core (`review3/A/core-wall-all.mjs`), the same rule finds the same six offending imports as on 28 September: `deliver.ts:28,29,47`, `wire-senders.ts:6`, `leads/runner/check.ts:7` and `start.ts:6`. `deliver.ts` also makes six direct table calls (`:241,466,474,510,546,762`).

**SQL is where the system grows, with no rule for it.** 24 migrations since 28 September add 6,173 lines. There are 302 functions (259 before), 106 of them defined in more than one migration (90; `people_list` 16 times), and 62 triggers (55) (`review3/A/sql-functions.mjs`). `CLAUDE.md:146` is still the one line on SQL doors.
gaps: **Dependency inversion.** The wall covers 46 of 75 core files. `wire-senders.ts:6` puts provider calls inside core, and `leads/cards.ts:126,213` name Apify's actors. `docs/architecture.md`'s package table says core holds no database client, which `deliver.ts:28` contradicts.

**Undeclared and unused dependencies.** `@supabase/supabase-js` is imported by `packages/core/src/deliver.ts:28` and four jobs modules (`broadcast-send.ts:8`, `context.ts:9`, `escalate.ts:5`, `ledger.ts:16`), and declared by neither package. Both declare `zod` and never import it. `knip.json:13,16` turns `dependencies` and `unlisted` off, and the hoisted linker (`.npmrc:4`) hides the gap.

**Unmeasured drift.** `.rpc(` outside `packages/db` went from 120 to 129, like for like (Reach out 6–7's `reach-out-leads.ts` 3 and `lead-lists.ts` 2, `vitals.ts` 2, and others), because the tables ratchet counts only `.from(` (`_ast.mjs:436`). Live SQL functions writing events went from 51 to 57.

**ADRs.** There is still no packaging note: `docs/debt.md:47-48` still waits for "a decision note", and core's dist is 1.88 MB, rewritten by 19 of the 84 commits since 28 September. Nothing decides SQL doors against core verbs. The note template has no Consequences (0022 alone has one) and no superseded-by, and the README says to edit a note in place (`docs/decisions/README.md:34`).

**Consistency.** There are two copies of the JSON logger: the edge's `lib/log.ts` and the dashboard's `server/log.ts`, the second new in #1332. The packages log positional console lines (`db/src/events.ts:198`). The shell grew to 132 JSX files and 55.2k lines (129 and 54.1k before), and 0015 is accepted but no surface has moved.

cats.name: Domain / Business Logic
cats.verdict: The category's largest structural defect is gone. `answerInbound` is now an 18-line order over phase modules and pure truth tables. Three more sagas became tables of steps (a line purchase, the diagnostics door, Stripe's events). But none of the one-derivation steps moved: the pause length still has five derivations, E.164 has two lengths in TypeScript and gained a SQL copy of each spelling, and the veto's words are typed eight times. Partners' terms still sit in two places, conversation transitions are still unguarded, and erasure still runs in a route. So the score holds, and the four small steps below would move it.
evidence: **The receptionist's order is readable (#1268).** `answer.ts:78-95` is the whole order: each gate returns the `GO` sentinel (`context.ts:29`) over one `Answering` record, and the no-side-effect decisions are truth tables in `steps.ts` and `reply-posture.ts`. The phases still read the clock 17 times (`dispatch.ts:112,140,171,177`, `model-turn.ts:39,80,89,95`, `unreadable.ts:29,48,64`), and `InboundPorts` (`ports.ts:192`) has no `now`, where conversations (`conversations/ports.ts:53`) and campaigns (`campaigns/ports.ts:94`) have one.

**One predicate where it matters, still.** `mayMessageFor` (`contracts/src/consent/consent.ts:83`) and `DELIVERY_REFUSALS` (`:108`) are single, and the send door reads `outreachRefusalOf` (`deliver.ts:403`, `reach-out/reach-out-rules.ts:25`). A person's state is one function (`people/person-state.ts:108`) that People and Ask both read (`ask/tools/read/people.ts:56`).

**The pause length is still derived five ways:** truthy at `core/src/inbound/context.ts:61` and `edge/api/whatsapp.ts:206`, `?? 24` at `retell-webhook.ts:401`, `>= 1` at `dashboard/src/server/verbs.ts:276`, and `> 0` at `contracts/src/config/policy.ts:270`. Its default is two constants, `PAUSE_MS` (`inbound/steps.ts:11`) and `PAUSE_HOURS_DEFAULT` (`policy.ts:245`).

**Ask still drafts a card for a person who texted STOP (defect 32).** `review3/A/probe-ask-reply.mjs` run at `1388f2cc6` gives "CARD: Reply to Ana" for `consent: opted_out, dnc: false`, and a refusal for `dnc: true` (`ask/tools/act/reply.ts:46`). Core then refuses the card (`conversations/reply.ts:297`).

**Sagas are tables.** `runLineSaga` has one handler per step (#1287, `channels/src/lines/lines-saga.ts`), the diagnostics door has ten report parts (#1280), and Stripe dispatches through `handlerOf` (`stripe-webhook.ts:377`, #1324). The 00254 fix (#1249) aligned three SQL counts of who is new, and a db test holds that case.
gaps: **One source of truth.** E.164 has two lengths in contracts itself: `E164` takes 7–15 digits (`workspace-config/business-profile.ts:179`, `shared/phone.ts:111`) and `normalizePhone` takes 8–15 (`shared/phone.ts:15`). cats.name: Separation of Concerns
cats.verdict: The route and the door separate more cleanly than on 28 September. Stripe's door is 32 lines over a handler table, every dashboard call to the edge goes through one bounded `callEdge`, provider calls leave through `providerFetch`, and the dashboard server logs through one logger under lint. The same four exceptions stand: erasure runs in its route file, the WhatsApp and Retell function doors still decide inline, four model clients bypass the provider layer, and core still carries HTTP statuses, table calls and console lines. No test requires a door to plan.
evidence: **The route pipeline is fixed and thin.** `route()` checks scope, role, spend, rate and input in that order (`apps/dashboard/src/server/route.ts:218-235`). The 172 route files have a median of 32 lines; 29 read through `server/readers`, 11 call core, and 45 call `.from` or `.rpc` directly (46 before).

**Doors over plans or tables.** The Stripe `POST` is 32 lines at cyclomatic 10 over `handlerOf` (`apps/edge/api/stripe-webhook.ts:53,377`; it was 256 lines, #1324). 10 of 51 edge doors call a `plan*()`. `whatsapp.ts` `POST` is still 186 lines at cyclomatic 51 and depth 10 (`:60`), and `retell-fn.ts` `POST` 279 at 37 (`:103`) (`review3/A/fn-metrics.mjs`).

**One way out to a provider, one way to the edge.** `providerFetch` (`packages/channels/src/provider-fetch.ts:211`) returns four outcomes, and a send not taken is held for a fresh job (`wire-senders.ts:77`). `callEdge` (`apps/dashboard/src/server/edge.ts`) bounds every JSON call to the edge and answers a named 503.

**The erasure saga is readable but still in the route.** `erasePerson` orders seven steps (`app/api/v1/contacts/[id]/route.ts:81-90`, #1312), and the route makes 6 direct `.from`/`.rpc` calls (`:123,134,137,231,313,324`) plus the service-role legs in `server/people/erasure.ts`.
**Pages do not fetch.** The `fetch(` scan in `repo/hygiene.test.mjs` holds `src/legacy` to the typed client (7 tests pass).
gaps: **Doors that decide inline.** `whatsapp.ts:60` routes, persists echoes, pauses and dispatches statuses in one handler, and repeats the pause derivation at `:206`. `retell-fn.ts:103` is unchanged. Nothing requires a door to call a plan or a handler table.

**Model calls beside the provider layer.** There are four `new Anthropic` clients (`google/review-reply.ts:22`, `leads/lead-wires.ts:67`, `model.ts:60`, `receptionist/brain.ts:33`) and a raw fetch in `admin/llm.ts:95`, outside `providerFetch`'s outcomes and breaker. `Provider` has no `anthropic` (`provider-fetch.ts:36`).

**Infrastructure in core.** 24 of core's 70 `AppError`s carry an HTTP status. `deliver.ts` and `messages/broadcast.ts` log 9 positional console lines (8 before). `deliver.ts:28` types a Supabase client.

**Orchestration packed into single functions.** `runAskTurn` is 490 lines at cyclomatic 71 (`server/ask/loop.ts:268`; 525/80 before). `reachOutClock` is 152 lines at depth 8 (`apps/edge/lib/reach-out/clock.ts:81`).
**Environment and formatting.** The dashboard reads `process.env` 49 times in 23 files, with no env module or lint rule, where the edge has both. Contracts hard-codes `"en-US"` 58 times (56 before).

cats.name: Data Flow
cats.verdict: Two of the four September steps started in #1332. A request is now named in `withRoute`, logged under that name and carried to the edge's admin doors, and TypeScript writes events through one typed, versioned writer. The id still stops at the job row, the webhook doors and the event ledger. SQL gained more sources: live functions writing events went from 51 to 57 and jobs from 8 to 9, three event kinds have writers on both sides with different shapes under one version, and there is still no current-schema snapshot or data-flow document.
evidence: **A request has a name.** `with-route.ts:94-98` mints it (`requestIdOf`, `channels/src/tokens/request-id.ts:18`), runs the handler under it and answers `x-request-id`. `edgeHeaders` carries it (`server/edge.ts:57-58`), and `authorizeAdmin` binds it on the edge (`apps/edge/lib/admin-auth.ts:62`, `lib/log.ts:47`). All 25 dashboard call sites to the edge, including Ask's stream (`ask/gateway.ts:95`), send it.

**One TypeScript event writer.** `emitEvent` and `recordEvent` (`packages/db/src/events.ts:176,189`) take the kind's category and version from `WRITES` (`:98`) and 00264's column. No TypeScript file but `events.ts` inserts into `events`. A failed write is still one positional `console.error` (`:198`), counted nowhere.

**Webhooks acknowledge only what the database took.** They answer 503 otherwise: `whatsapp.ts:243`, `apify-webhook.ts:62,111`, plus Retell, Stripe and Resend. A provider call's outcome now drives the retry (`provider-fetch.ts:211`).

**SQL is still a second source for jobs and events.** 9 live SQL functions insert jobs, all the lead finder's; `lead_search_import` and `lead_rounds_notify` in 00242 are new. 57 insert events (51 on 28 September), and 65 migration files do (61). 106 functions are defined in more than one migration (`review3/A/sql-live-writers.mjs`, `sql-functions.mjs`).

**The three flows, traced at `1388f2cc6`:**
- **An inbound WhatsApp message, about 14 hops.** `api/whatsapp.ts:60` → `lib/whatsapp/inbound.ts:28` → `ports.ts` → core `answer.ts:78` and its phases → `persist.ts` (SQL `ingest_inbound`) → `receptionist/brain.ts` (its own Anthropic client) → `persist.ts:244` → `deliver.ts:569` → `wire-senders.ts:97` → `channels/whatsapp.ts:273` → `providerFetch("meta", breaker "count")`. No request id: no webhook door binds one.
- **An operator's reply, about 16 hops.** The route and `withRoute` (id minted) → core `replyToConversation` → `replyPorts` (`core-ports.ts:128`, claims and inserts) → `scheduleJob` (`jobs/src/schedule.ts:18`). The id stops there. → `api/jobs/tick.ts` → `handlers.ts:47` → `deliver()` → `putOnWire` (`wire-senders.ts:187`) → `providerFetch` → Meta, then back through the status webhook and realtime to the page.
- **A lead-finder run, about 15 hops.** `lead-searches/route.ts:51` → SQL `lead_search_create`, which inserts the job (the id stops) → tick → `lead-pipeline.ts` → core `runner/start.ts` → `channels/leads/apify.ts:117` `providerFetch("apify")` → `apify-webhook.ts` → SQL `lead_collect_commit` inserts the next jobs → `runner/check.ts` → the judge through `lead-wires.ts:67`'s own Anthropic client → SQL → the Leads page.
gaps: **The id stops at the queue.** `scheduleJob`'s row, the event row and the SQL job and event writers carry no request id. `bindRequestId` is called only in `authorizeAdmin`, so the webhook, cron and tick lines have none. The id is a header, not signed into the edge token.

**Two sources for jobs and events.** 9 live SQL functions insert jobs and there is no `schedule_job()`. 57 live SQL functions insert events outside `WRITES`, and three kinds (`contact.added`, `contact.consent_changed`, `platform.acted`) have writers on both sides (new defect below).
**No current schema.** 106 functions are defined in more than one migration, `people_list` 16 times; the live definition is whichever file came last.

**No data-flow document.** Nothing traces the reader layer, the two browser caches (`legacy-bridge/surface-cache.ts`, `read-cache.ts`) or the request id's reach. `docs/takeover.md:84` still says there is no correlation id at all.

steps.t: Carry the request id into the job row and the event row (a column each, beside `version`). Bind a name in every edge door: the provider's delivery id at a webhook, the job id at the tick.
Give each event kind one writer, or have SQL writers state their version. Log `emit_event_failed` as JSON and count it in the health sweep.
Add one SQL `schedule_job()` for the 9 live SQL job writers, beside `scheduleJob`.
Generate a current-schema snapshot in CI, so each function's live definition is one file.
Write `docs/data-flow.md`: the three flows above with their hops, the readers, the caches, and where the request id reaches.

bullets.e: Named at `with-route.ts:94`, then the `route()` pipeline (`route.ts:218-235`); the name ends at the job row.
One reader layer for pages and Ask (`server/readers`); no data-flow document.
Postgres holds state and realtime only signals a re-read (`surface-runner.ts:308`); conversation state has 3 writing layers.
Package direction held by `.npmrc:5` and `lint-boundaries.test.mjs` (19 pass).
One typed TypeScript writer (`events.ts:189`); 57 live SQL writers; 3 kinds written from both sides.
Four provider outcomes, `callEdge`'s named 503, webhook 503s; `emit_event_failed` is only a positional log (`events.ts:198`).
Session or bearer verified in `withRoute`; a per-door signed token to the edge (`edge.ts:60`, `admin-auth.ts:66`).
`route()` scope, role and spend on the session client, so RLS is the enforcement (`route.ts:218-231`).
299 live SQL functions, 106 defined more than once, no snapshot.
`providerFetch` for 7 providers; model calls through 4 own clients; 3 raw fetches left (`whatsapp.ts:382`, `voice-retell.ts:631`, `admin/llm.ts:95`).
Every provider webhook answers 503 for what the database did not take (`whatsapp.ts:243`, `apify-webhook.ts:111`).
One TypeScript door (`schedule.ts:18`) plus 9 live SQL inserters; no request id in either.
Two browser caches, each explained in its own header (`surface-cache.ts:1`, `read-cache.ts:1`); no document of the rules.
The reply goes through core with an idempotency key (`core-ports.ts:143`); 45 routes write or read tables directly.
Sends leave only through `deliver()` (`deliver.ts:569`); `deliver.ts` itself writes tables inside core.
Postgres, read through one reader layer by pages and Ask; realtime is a signal (`surface-runner.ts:308`).
521 table names outside `packages/db` held; 129 `.rpc(` calls not held.

bullets.b: Traceability (user → API → logic → database → response without unrelated abstractions)
bullets.e: The request id reaches dashboard lines and edge admin doors (`admin-auth.ts:62`), not jobs, webhooks, events or the packages' console lines.

cats.name: Database Architecture
cats.verdict: The discipline held across 24 more migrations: four new tables, all with RLS and a row in the tenancy matrix; all 246 definer functions pin their path; and the scale lane's indexes and reads are measured in their headers. The structural gaps stand. A member's message insert checks its own tenant but not its parent's, the only composite keys are the reach-out chain, `lock_timeout` is still a habit (36 of 238 files), and production again took a migration from a branch with no ledger check.
evidence: Four tables since 28 Sep (`partner_invitations` 00225:43, `page_vitals` 00255:26, `person_moments` 00259:78, `erasure_keying` 00263:55) each enable RLS and sit in the matrix (`tooling/scripts/tests/database/tenancy.db.test.mjs:341-353,519,631,655-656`). The matrix fails on any table it leaves out (`:694`).

Static scan of all 238 files (`review3/D/definers.mjs`): 297 functions, 246 SECURITY DEFINER, 0 with an unpinned path. `privileges.db.test.mjs:203` holds that in the required Database check, and `:189,197` hold anon and trigger callability.

The scale lane (#1328) reads by index: `contact_identities`/`conversations`/`escalations`/`deals` by person (`00253:31-40`), `lead_places` by lead (`00256:30`), and the latest inbound per channel (`00257:30-32`), each under `set local lock_timeout = '3s'` with a self-check (`00257:20-26`). `newest_messages` is invoker with `search_path = ''` and bounded (`00258:22-45`). `person_moments` is kept by triggers with a recompute (`00259:153-186`) and a db test (`people/moments/person-moments.db.test.mjs`).

Lifecycle: `purge-page-vitals` deletes after 30 days (`00255:79`); `delete_my_account` now pauses, marks and closes a workspace it empties (`00262:70-80`). `idempotency_keys` still has no purge (0 delete/cron lines in migrations), and `jobs` still has no tenant index (its indexes: `00002:209-210`, `00078:50`, `00098:53`, `00127:25`, `00135:28`, `00140:433`, `00222:147`).

Drift: 36 of 238 files set `lock_timeout` (9 of the 24 new; `00228` alters `playbooks`, `broadcasts` and `reach_out_sends` without it, and `00262:21` alters `tenants`). `migrations.test.mjs:32-59` checks one tree only. `00261:27-29` records that 00242 was applied to production before its branch merged, and `00245:3-4` was renumbered 'above the production ledger's head' by hand.
gaps: Referential integrity: `messages_acting_member_insert` (`00260:19-31`) checks the row's tenant, role, sender, status and now `media`, but never that `conversation_id` or `contact_id` belong to that tenant. Foreign-key checks ignore RLS, and `00259`'s trigger and the edge's orphan sweep act on the pair (new defect). The only composite `(tenant_id, id)` keys are the chain's (`00183:59-69`).
Constraints: no column-level INSERT grant in 238 files; `privileges.db.test.mjs:179` fences UPDATE columns only.

Lifecycle:
- `idempotency_keys` is never purged.
- `jobs` has no tenant index.
- `tooling/scripts/ops/delete-tenant.mjs` still leaves the `media/<tenant>/` objects.
- An emptied workspace is kept with its customers' data and no erase clock (`00262:15`: 'the platform erases it on its own rule, later'; nothing reads `left_empty_at` but billing).
Migration safety: no lint for `lock_timeout`, no checksum manifest, and no check that production's ledger equals main, while numbers are chosen by hand around production's head.

cats.name: Async / Concurrency
cats.verdict: Every provider and edge call now has a bound, a typed outcome and a retry rule keyed on it (#1332), and a send the provider did not take, or whose credentials could not be read, waits for a fresh job instead of failing (#1326, #1332). What held the score at 8 is still open: no type-aware promise lint, no database or client-level timeout, inbound messages to one thread answered independently, a broadcast assembled in three writes, and nothing that fails the next bare `fetch(`.
evidence: **Every server fetch is bounded: 7 of 7 sites carry a signal (16 bare on 28 Sep)** (`review3/E/fetch-timeouts.mjs`). Provider calls leave through `providerFetch`, whose `timeoutMs` is required (`packages/channels/src/provider-fetch.ts:58-60,183`), and the dashboard reaches the edge through `callEdge`, 20 s by default (`apps/dashboard/src/server/edge.ts:72,84-123`). `provider-fetch.test.mjs` passes 6/6 and `dashboard-edge.test.mjs:79` 5/5.

**Retry by outcome** (#1332): `ok`, `refused`, `retryable` and `unknown` are mapped from status and throw (`provider-fetch.ts:115-131`). A call asks again only when the answer is `retryable`, or `unknown` on an idempotent call, and never after a timeout. Waits are 250 ms doubling, with Retry-After honoured under a 2 s cap and a deadline (`:224-234`). There is one breaker per provider: 5 faults hold the provider for 30 s (`:79-81,143-161`), and sends are `breaker: "count"`, always made and only counted (`whatsapp.ts:280`, `email-resend.ts:143`).

**A send not taken waits** (#1332, #1326): `putOnWire` throws `NotTakenError` for a `retryable` send when the caller asked to hold it (`packages/core/src/wire-senders.ts:202`), and throws `WireUnavailableError` for a credentials read that failed (`:31-32,189`). `sendQueued` then hands the send to a fresh job on `SEND_RETRY_WAITS_MS` 1/3/10/30 min, and the last try is not held (`packages/core/src/messages/send.ts:26,91,100-101,119-145`). `core-send-path.test.mjs:557` and `deliver.test.mjs:453` pass, 15/15 and 48/48.

Claims made in the database still hold. The reply claims its key first (`packages/core/src/conversations/reply.ts:332-351`; `core-reply.test.mjs` 19/19). A second live line is refused by index (`00195:23-25`; `lines-door.test.mjs` 23/23). `claim_due_jobs` is `SKIP LOCKED` (`00098:63-86`), and ingest is serialised per identity (`00110:131-133`).

**Still open:** `createServiceClient` sets no fetch timeout (`packages/db/src/service-client.ts:15-19`), and no migration sets a `statement_timeout` for the service role. Lint still parses without types (`eslint.config.mjs:311-313`). Server code holds 85 `.catch(() => {}|undefined|null)`, the same as on 28 Sep.
gaps: **Transactions and keys:** a broadcast is three writes with a compensating fail (`packages/core/src/campaigns/assemble.ts:12-34`), and its POST takes no idempotency key (`apps/dashboard/app/api/v1/broadcasts/route.ts:34-44`).
**Backoff has no jitter anywhere:** the ledger's fixed waits (`packages/jobs/src/ledger.ts:141-165`), `SEND_RETRY_WAITS_MS`, `BROADCAST_THROTTLE_WAITS_MS` and `providerFetch`'s doubling.

steps.t: A lint rule or source scan that refuses `fetch(` outside `providerFetch`/`callEdge`/the Ask gateway; a fetch timeout in `createServiceClient`; a `statement_timeout` for `service_role`.
Type-aware lint on the server trees for `no-floating-promises` and `no-misused-promises` (move 4).
Serialise inbound work per conversation, so a newer customer message supersedes a reply that has not gone yet.
Assemble a broadcast (run, recipients, job) in one SQL function, and give the sending POSTs an idempotency key.
Keep the last owner in the database: a trigger on `memberships`, or the count under a row lock; add jitter to every retry wait.

cats.name: Event Architecture
cats.verdict: The ledger now has one writer: each kind declares its data's type, its category and its version in one table, all 47 TypeScript writes go through it, and each row carries `version` (#1332, 00264). Contracts and versioning moved from absent to present at compile time. Durability, consumers, replay and dead letters have not moved: a TypeScript emit that fails is still a log line, and nothing reads the ledger as a stream.
evidence: **One typed writer** (#1332): `TableData` gives 47 kinds their data types (`packages/db/src/events.ts:28-88`), and `WRITES` gives each its category and version, never the caller (`:98-145`). `recordEvent` returns the error to a writer that needs the row (`:176-186`); `emitEvent` logs `emit_event_failed` and returns (`:189-199`). 42 `emitEvent` and 6 `recordEvent` calls; 0 inserts into `events` outside `events.ts` (grep).

**Versioned** (00264): `events.version smallint not null default 1` on the partitioned parent (`00264_an_event_says_which_version_of_its_kind_it_is.sql:15`). Every kind is at 1, and nothing reads the column.

**Held by tests:** `events.type-test.ts` proves every written kind is one `EVENT_KINDS` declares; `event-writer.test.mjs` passes 2/2, including that the category and version come from the table; `event-kinds.test.mjs` passes 2/2 and now reads `recordEvent` too. There are 94 kinds (90 on 28 Sep), and 65 migrations emit inside the transaction (61).

Consumers of provider events stay idempotent: the wamid gate (`00002:109-110`), Stripe's `claimed`/`applied` lease (`00194`), Apify collect-once (`00140:433`), email ingest once (`00135`) and a reply read once per stage (`00222:146-148`). After #1324's split, Stripe's completion step runs as a returned thunk (`apps/edge/api/stripe-webhook.ts:71-77`).
gaps: **Contracts are compile-time only:** there is no runtime schema, and four kinds are wholly open: `broadcast.sent` and `usage.ask_tokens` are `Open`; `playbook.run` and `usage.llm_tokens` are `Record<string, unknown>` (`events.ts:32,73,83-84`). Meta's family is open by design.
**Durability:** a failed TypeScript emit is a console line (`events.ts:198`), with no outbox, retry, alert or dead letter.
**Consumers and replay:** none. The ledger is read by ad-hoc queries (Ask's day sum `00240:23`, a person's door `00250:172`), never by a cursor. Record kinds are kept for ever and never rolled up.
**Versioning is written but not read:** no reader branches on `version`, and no test says when a kind's shape change must raise it.

steps.t: A zod schema per kind checked at the writer (or in a test over every emitter's call), and a rule that a shape change raises `version`.
Move the remaining best-effort emits into the state change's SQL or through the jobs ledger, and alert on `emit_event_failed`.
Daily rollups as idempotent consumers of events with a cursor, and a replay script over the partitions.

cats.verdict: Still a good single ledger, and its failure modes are more honest than on 28 Sep. The tick binds each wire on its own (#1330). A send whose credentials could not be read, or which the provider did not take, waits for a fresh job (#1326, #1332). Each heartbeat logs how late each kind's first claim came (0018, step 1). The queue is unchanged: one lane ordered by due time, no fairness, fixed waits with no jitter, no requeue, no tenant index, and an unknown kind still fails at once. Two broadcast paths misbehave (new defects).
evidence: **One lane, unchanged:** `claim_due_jobs` orders every tenant and kind by `due_at` alone (`supabase/migrations/00098_time_lives_in_the_row.sql:74`). Decision 0018 is accepted with only step 1 built: 'steps 2 and 3 follow, and step 4 only if step 1's numbers ask' (`docs/decisions/0018-a-reply-goes-first.md:3`). **Lateness measured** (#1205): `noteLate` keeps each kind's worst first-claim wait (`packages/jobs/src/tick.ts:71-82`), and the heartbeat logs it as `late_ms_<kind>` (`apps/edge/api/jobs/tick.ts:150-153`); `jobs-tick-door.test.mjs:838` holds it. It is a log field only, with no threshold, alert or stored series.

**Wires bound one at a time** (#1330, #1326): a mailbox read that throws becomes email's `WireUnavailable` alone (`apps/edge/api/jobs/tick.ts:84-102`), and WhatsApp and SMS reads return `unavailable`, not null (`apps/edge/lib/tenant-runtime.ts:297-333`, `apps/edge/lib/sms/sms.ts:172-182`). `jobs-tick-door.test.mjs:656`: 'a mailbox that could not be read unbinds email's wire and nothing else'; 11/11 pass.

Retry and settlement still hold. Kinds that speak to a person are never re-run after an unknown outcome (`packages/jobs/src/ledger.ts:87,111-115`). Seven kinds retry on fixed two-step waits (`:141-165`). Fresh-job resends are bounded (`packages/core/src/messages/send.ts:26`), and a broadcast resumes at most `MAX_RESUMES` = 5 times (`ledger.ts:84`). `purge_jobs` keeps done rows 7 days and failed rows 90 (`00215:15,33`). `jobs-tick`, `jobs-ledger`, `ops-hygiene` and `core-broadcast` pass 21/21, 20/20, 8/8 and 24/24.

cats.name: Scalability
cats.verdict: The high defect is closed: the sweeps read only what is due, a paused workspace holds no place, and the backlog alarm counts only due work (#1323, 00245). A wave of reads now goes by index: a person's rows, listings, a channel's latest word, the Inbox's newest messages (#1247, #1226, #1328). The ceilings that remain are capacity rather than starvation: 25 moments and 25 reach-out steps an hour platform-wide in one serial sweep, one job lane, 23 table subscriptions per tab, and People and Today still reading a workspace's whole history on each call.
evidence: **Due-aware sweeps** (#1323): `playbooks_due` and `calendars_due` judge due-ness in SQL by each workspace's zone and leave out a paused workspace (`supabase/migrations/00245_the_sweeps_read_only_what_is_due.sql:65-84`, `:78`). `due_total` makes `remaining` exact. Any page row not run is stamped to the back, and yielded reach-out steps are counted (`apps/edge/api/cron/playbooks.ts:54-134`). `cron-playbooks-door.test.mjs` passes 24/24, including 26 paused moments beside two due ones (`:567`) and the reach-out twin (`:881`, `:912`).

**Reads by index:** a person's rows (`00253`), People's messages and doors, and first replies read once per row (`00250`), each report day in one pass (`00251`), listings (`00256`), a channel's latest word (`00257`). The Inbox reads each thread's newest messages through its own index, capped at 100 per thread and 4,000 in all (`00258:1-19`).

**Still whole-history:** `people_list` aggregates each person's messages and orders everyone by last contact before `limit … offset` (`00250:222-235,299-301`), and `everyoneIn` pages through all of it (`packages/db/src/repositories/people.ts:74`). `metrics_summary` scans every contact with two subqueries each (`00254:69-85`). `person_moments` is kept by triggers, but 'Nothing reads the table yet' (`00259:5-6`).

**Realtime unchanged:** one channel per tab with 23 `postgres_changes` bindings (`packages/db/src/realtime.ts:24-53,79-97`). Decision 0019 is 'decided, not built' (`docs/decisions/0019-the-database-tells-each-workspace-what-changed.md:3`).

**Throughput unchanged:** 25 moments and 25 reach-out steps an hour, platform-wide (`apps/edge/lib/ops/sweep-rotation.ts:54-55`, hourly at `:05`, `00048:120`); batches of 25 sends 300 ms apart; one job lane (`00098:74`). A number's tier is checked per run, not across a day's runs (`packages/core/src/campaigns/create-broadcast.ts:145`).
gaps: **Sweeps:** one serial function runs at most 25 due moments and 25 reach-out steps an hour for the whole platform. Past that the alarm is honest, but the work is not fanned out as jobs.
**Database:** `people_list` and `metrics_summary` grow with a workspace's history; no rollups; offset paging (0021 steps 2–5 unbuilt).
**API and queue:** 23 table subscriptions per open tab (0019 unbuilt); one job lane with no tenant fairness; no load test.
**Storage:** `idempotency_keys` is never purged; record events and their monthly partitions are kept for ever; the text index is platform-wide GIN with no tenant in its key (`00219:27-31`).
**Backpressure:** a Graph 429 stops and reschedules a broadcast, but a connection that never opened burns its recipients (new defect).

cats.name: External Integrations
cats.verdict: **One transport now carries almost every provider call.** `providerFetch` bounds each call, never throws, says one of four outcomes, retries only what cannot be done twice and keeps a breaker per provider; server fetches without a bound fell from 16 to 0, and a credentials, line or mailbox read that fails makes a queued reply wait instead of failing it. What is left is words and edges: Meta and Twilio codes past the throttle and 21610 still reach the owner as “HTTP 400”, the webhook's own reply is not retried by outcome and caches a vault blip as “no credentials”, and a broadcast fails its whole list when Graph cannot be reached.
evidence: **`providerFetch`** (`packages/channels/src/provider-fetch.ts:211-235`, #1332): a status or a throw becomes `ok | refused | retryable | unknown` (`:115-131`); asks again only a `retryable` answer, or an `unknown` one for an idempotent call, honouring Retry-After up to 2 s inside a deadline (`:224-234`); a breaker per provider opens after 5 faults for 30 s (`:79-81,146-156`), and a send to a person (`breaker: "count"`) is always made and only counted (`:161`). 17 call sites (7 in the edge, 10 in channels) plus the per-provider helpers over it (`retell()` `voice/voice-retell.ts:211`, `twilioRequest` `lines/lines-twilio.ts:72`, `resendRequest`, `placesFetch`, `postGraph` `whatsapp.ts:273`). `ops/provider-fetch.test.mjs` 6/6, the breaker and the never-held send among them.

**Timeouts, measured** (AST over the edge, the dashboard's server and app, `packages/*/src`, `apps/mobile`; review3/F/measure.mjs): 21 fetch sites (69 on 28 Sep), and server-side sites without a bound 0 (16 on 28 Sep: the 10 dashboard→edge calls are 20 `callEdge` sites, `apps/dashboard/src/server/edge.ts:84-123`, 20 s default, a 503 `edge_timeout`/`edge_unreachable`; Retell's 4 reads, diag's `debug_token` `apps/edge/api/diag.ts:197`). The 8 left are browser or phone code (`client/api.ts:194,195,280`, `signup/page.tsx:74,136`, `GoogleSignIn.tsx:16`, `LegacyApp.tsx:354`, `mobile/src/app/_layout.tsx:39`). `edge/dashboard-edge.test.mjs` 5/5.

**What a send came to, run end to end** over the real tick route and the suite's fake database (review3/F/probe-tick-blips.mjs): a vault read that fails leaves the reply queued with a fresh job in 60 s and pages `wire_unavailable:whatsapp`, nobody flagged (A, #1326); a mailbox read that fails unbinds email only and the WhatsApp reply leaves (B, #1330); a Graph timeout is `failed` with `outcome: unknown` and the owner reads “it may have gone; check the thread before sending it again” (C, #1332); a texting-line read that fails leaves the WhatsApp reply alone (D); a Graph 429 stays queued for a fresh job, nobody told (E: `NotTakenError`, `packages/core/src/wire-senders.ts:202`, `SEND_RETRY_WAITS_MS` 1/3/10/30 min `messages/send.ts:26`).

**Retell's call read says what happened** (#1322): `getCall` answers found, not_found, unavailable or auth (`packages/channels/src/voice/voice-retell.ts:312-360`); the recordings sweep defers without spending a try (`apps/edge/api/cron/calls.ts:212-233`) and answers 503 `provider_unauthorized` for a refused key (`:403-409`). `cron/cron-doors-b.test.mjs` 26/26, `voice/calls/call-lifecycle.test.mjs` 14/14.

**The webhook doors still tell “could not read” from “no”**: voice 503s (`retell-webhook-door.test.mjs` 21/21), Stripe's found/gone/unreadable with a leased claim kept through #1324's split (`apps/edge/api/stripe-webhook.ts:235-250`, `billing-webhook.test.mjs` 16/16); Twilio 21610 is recorded as the carrier's opt-out (`packages/core/src/deliver.ts:619-627`, `sms/sms-door.test.mjs` 11/11).
gaps: **Provider codes past the throttle reach the owner as numbers** (probe-tick-blips F, G, H): Meta 131047 (the 24-hour window) is “could not be delivered (HTTP 400)”; 190 (an expired token, the workspace's own) is “(HTTP 401)” and pages the platform as `provider_auth:whatsapp`; a 503 is recorded `outcome: unknown` yet told “HTTP 503”, not “may have gone” (`packages/core/src/messages/send.ts:252-256` reads `mayHaveGone` only at status 0). 131026, Twilio 21211 and 30007 are not branched anywhere (grep: 0 sites).

**The webhook's credentials read caches a blip as “none”**: `resolveWaCredentials` returns null on a vault error (`apps/edge/lib/tenant-runtime.ts:154-157`) and `loadTenantRuntime` caches it for 10 minutes (`:81,255`); run: a second load with the vault back still has no credentials (review3/F/probe-runtime-creds-cache.mjs). Every receptionist reply on that instance fails meanwhile (defect 8, partly).

**The breaker is per provider per instance, and silent**: nothing logs its opening, `breakerOf` (`provider-fetch.ts:94`) is read by no code, `breaker_open` is named by no caller, and there is no pause per workspace and channel.

**Isolation and provider-agnostic interfaces, unchanged in place**: 14 provider request paths still live in the edge, now on channels' transport (Meta 5: `diag.ts:197`, `whatsapp/meta-graph.ts:43`, `meta-templates.ts:60,200,249`; Twilio 6: `sms/sms.ts:89`, `lines/a2p-refile.ts:67,176,244`, `a2p-register.ts:311`, `a2p-sync.ts:41`; the pager's Resend `ops/notify.ts:101`; Expo `ops/push.ts:72`; Anthropic `api/admin/llm.ts:95`), APNs is its own HTTP/2 wire (`ops/apns.ts:83`); `wamid` names every provider's id (31 sites), a text arrives as a `WaRawMessage` (`packages/channels/src/lines/sms.ts:16`), core's lead port is typed `ApifyClient` (`packages/core/src/leads/ports.ts:9,314`). No lint or test stops a new bare `fetch`.

cats.name: AI / LLM Architecture
cats.verdict: Ask Rewired 5–6 made Ask the best-instrumented path in the product: each answer keeps its turn exactly as sent with a sha256 of its system, tools and config, every round names why its cache missed, the day budget is one SQL sum, and the nightly checks Ask's cache and first words against lines. The platform layer did not move: 6 model ids in 10 files, four SDK clients and a raw-fetch gateway, no fallback on a 529 or 5xx, no dollars on any row, and evals still run by hand on the production key.
evidence: **Ask's turn is kept as sent, with a prompt hash:** `rawTurn` stores the last request's messages, the model and `prefix`, a sha256 of system, tools, tool choice and output config (`apps/dashboard/src/server/ask/memory.ts:424-460`, `:468-471`), on the answer row at `content.raw` (`turn-end.ts:163-166`, #1261); a warm follow-up replays it byte for byte when the model and prefix match (`memory.ts:367-383`, #1282).

**Per-turn telemetry:** `AskTurnShape` stores model, effort, tokens with cache reads and writes, `cache_miss` per round from the API's diagnostics and the edge hop (`turn-end.ts:112-143`, `sse.ts:121-133`, #1316); the nightly runs `ops/ask-day.mjs --check` on production's rows and opens an issue when the median cache hit falls under its line or first text crosses 6 s (`.github/workflows/nightly-e2e.yml:63-86`, `ask-stats.mjs:53-73`, #1319).

**The registry holds:** 20 tools (9 reads, 11 acts, `ask/tools/registry.ts:60-94`), each call parsed by the role's own zod before any handler runs (`registry.ts:320-347`), tools offered per role (`tools/offer.ts:44-67`); Ask's profile is one list the edge's allow-list is built from (`packages/contracts/src/ask/ask-model.ts:32-65`, `apps/edge/lib/ask-gateway.ts:189`).

**The receptionist is structured and split:** constrained decoding then `parseBrainOutput`, a capped or unparseable answer sends the holding reply and escalates (`apps/edge/lib/receptionist/brain.ts:164-219`); the prompt is thirteen sections in a table (`contracts/src/config/workspace-config/compose.ts:277`, #1269) and `answerInbound` is seven phase modules, none over the limits (`packages/core/src/inbound/*`, #1268).

**Evals grew, still manual:** Ask 80 → 90 cases, 18 must-never, 10 with a second turn judged in the same thread (`tooling/evals/ask-cases.json`, #1256); the WhatsApp set is still 14 with no injection, refund or currency case (`tooling/evals/whatsapp-cases.json`); `ask-turn.test.mjs` 77 → 104 tests over a scripted round.
gaps: **No model layer:** 6 ids in 10 source files, unchanged (`templates.ts:41`, `model-json.ts:27`, `ask-gateway.ts:189,195`, `review-reply.ts:14`, `brain.ts:20`, `lead-judge.ts:30`, `voice-provision.ts:32,54` incl. `gpt-4.1`, `ask-model.ts:32`, `note-suggest.ts:22`, `reach-out-opening.ts:23`); 4 SDK clients (`brain.ts:33`, `review-reply.ts:22`, `lead-wires.ts:67`, `model.ts:60`) plus the raw fetch (`api/admin/llm.ts:33`); providerFetch (#1332) carries no model call.

**No fallback, no retry on overload:** the gateway forwards any upstream status (`api/admin/llm.ts:105-115`); the dashboard files everything but its own 429/503 as `bad_request` (`ask/gateway.ts:117-128`), so a 529 reads "The model refused the question" (`ask/loop.ts:212-215`). Only the lead judge uses the server-side fallback (`packages/channels/src/leads/lead-judge.ts:29,74-79`).

**Cost is tokens, never dollars:** dollars exist only in ops scripts (`tooling/scripts/ops/ask-day.mjs:32-35`); the receptionist drops cache tokens (`brain.ts:177-179`); the reply reader keeps no usage (`reach-out/reply-read.ts:57`); the budget sums input plus output, not cache writes (`00240_ask_counts_its_day_in_one_sum.sql:19-22`); usage rows are purged at 30 days (`contracts/src/workspace/retention.ts:14,52-53`).

**Prompt versioning is Ask's alone:** the receptionist stamps its model only (`contracts/src/config/brain.ts:152-161`); `settings.changed` keeps fields and the config version, never values (`packages/db/src/events.ts:82`), so a past reply's prompt cannot be rebuilt.

**No failure-rate alarm:** the nightly line judges cache hit and first text, not failed turns (`ask-stats.mjs:61-64`); the receptionist pages only when the key is missing (`packages/core/src/inbound/model-turn.ts:130-152`), a `brain_failed` storm escalates threads one by one.

steps.t: One model port by purpose (id, fallback, timeout, retries, max tokens) over the four clients and the gateway; every call writes tokens, cache tokens and list-price dollars to a kept row, the reply reader, the reach-out check and the notes sweep included; `REACH_OUT_MODEL` reads `NOTE_SUGGEST_MODEL`.
Retry once on a fallback model for 529, 5xx and timeouts at the gateway, and classify upstream 429/5xx as unreachable in `ask/gateway.ts`.

A nightly eval on a sandbox key against the e2e workspace with the scripts' all-pass gates; receptionist cases for injection, refunds, euros, pounds, pesos and multi-turn; add a failed-turn rate to the nightly's Ask line and a brain_failed rate page.
Stamp the receptionist's composed-prompt hash and config version on its message meta, and keep settings history with values.

cats.name: AI Agent Safety / Reliability
cats.verdict: Ask's data got tighter: a removed member can no longer read their threads, an erased person is scrubbed from Ask by name, and settings and policy audits finally reach the ledger. The customer-facing receptionist is unchanged: no money intent or rule, a dollar-and-peso price guard, no injection rule, an uncapped profile name in a system block, new workspaces on auto, and Google review auto-replies that keep posting for a paused or ended workspace.
evidence: **Ask never acts:** every act builds a card; a commit goes through the verb's own route marked `via: "ask"` and an undo names `undo_of` (`apps/dashboard/src/legacy-bridge/ask/commit.ts:51-105`); an action a role may not use is refused before its handler (`ask/tools/registry.ts:326-329`).

**Ask's memory is fenced by membership and erasure:** reads require the row's own user AND a current membership (`supabase/migrations/00236_a_person_reads_ask_only_while_a_member.sql:15-30`, #1264); an erased person's threads lose messages naming them and every raw that holds them (`00238_a_person_is_scrubbed_from_ask_by_name.sql:12-26`, #1284; `tests/people/erasure/erasure-ask-scrub.db.test.mjs`, 5 tests, nightly only).

**Audits land now:** settings and policy changes were written on the session, which may not insert into events, so they never reached the ledger; both are written as the service role through the typed writer (`apps/dashboard/src/server/workspace/settings-write.ts:31-48`, `app/api/v1/policies/route.ts:43`, #1332), with a version per kind (00264).

**Fences that hold:** Ask's rule that a customer's message never instructs (`ask/prompt.ts:83`); `<places>`, `<conversation>`, `<record>` and `<reply>` fences (`contracts/src/leads/lead-judge.ts:144`, `notes/note-suggest.ts:96`, `reach-out/reach-out-opening.ts:60-91`, `reach-out/reach-out-replies.ts:129,172`) with a planted "Ignore the instructions above" fixture (`tooling/scripts/fixtures/replies/replies.json:401`).

**Spend guards on the new paths:** the reply reader and the 0017 draft ask `workspaceMaySpend` and a day cap (`apps/edge/lib/reach-out/reply-read.ts:59-63`, `reply-draft.ts:67-72`); the draft is never sent by the model (`reply-draft.ts:1-12`).
gaps: **Money (defect 5):** `BRAIN_INTENTS` has no money intent (`packages/contracts/src/config/brain.ts:18-27`); the composed prompt has 0 of refund, discount, money, deposit on WhatsApp or voice (probe `review3/H/price-probe.mjs`); `money: ["never"]` (`policy-classes.ts:130`) is read by nothing at runtime while the pane says "always goes to you" (`:57`) and `README.md:18-19` says the prompt says so.

**Price guard (defect 6):** unchanged (`contracts/src/config/policy.ts:11-19`): misses €45, 45€, £30, 45 euros, 45 EUR, USD 45, 450 MXN, spelled-out prices, 20% off (probe); handoff lines English and salon-worded (`packages/core/src/inbound/steps.ts:121,131,133`); Google review auto-replies post unchecked (`apps/edge/lib/google/review-answers.ts:103-117`).

**Receptionist injection:** no rule line (probe); the profile name enters a system block uncapped (`packages/channels/src/whatsapp.ts:191` → `packages/db/src/repositories/thread.ts:352,441` → `apps/edge/lib/receptionist/brain.ts:158`); review replies quote the review with no rule (`contracts/src/google/review-reply.ts:93-99`).

**Data boundaries and idempotency:** 5 act lookups resolve by id through RLS alone (defect 26, script `review3/H/ask-lookups.sh`); only the reply card carries an idempotency key (`contracts/src/ask-proposals/inbox.ts:70`); the reply card ignores `consent = opted_out` (`ask/tools/act/reply.ts:46`), refused only at commit (`packages/core/src/conversations/reply.ts:297`).

**Pause does not reach reviews:** `connectionsDue` selects every connection (`apps/edge/lib/google/listing-check.ts:170-181`) and `answerNewReviews` reads only the reviews mode (`review-answers.ts:88`), so a billing-paused or 00262-ended workspace keeps auto-posting (new defect).

steps.t: A `money` intent mapped to the locked class, a prompt rule on both channels, an EN/ES deterministic detector in layer 2, receptionist eval cases; correct the README and the pane.
Widen `PRICE_PATTERNS` (€, £, codes before and after, MXN, spelled-out, percentages), localise the handoff lines, and run the guard on review auto-replies, the 0017 draft and the Ask card.
An injection rule in the composer, the profile name capped and quoted as data, the review fenced like `<reply>`.

`.eq("tenant_id")` on the last 5 lookups, `isOptedOutContact` in the reply card, the proposal id as every card's idempotency key, a veto window by default, and the review sweep skipping paused and ended workspaces.

cats.name: Testing Architecture
cats.verdict: Broader and still behavioural: 7,104 tests in 685 files, 101 stack suites, type tests that fail the compile, and every Wave E split kept its behaviour tests. The four blind spots named on 28 Sep have not moved: the replay's gate skipped the database suites on 11 main commits that changed what they load, the fake has no constraints, nothing pins the time zone, nothing measures coverage, and the nightly has now failed on each of its last four scheduled runs.
evidence: **7,104 tests in 685 files, 0 failing** (6,543 pass, 561 skip without credentials: `lead3/test.log`). By `review3/I1/test-kinds.mjs`: 571 files execute source (540 on 28 Sep), 13 only read it (13), 163 drive handlers over `_fake-db.mjs` (158), 386 tests named REGRESSION (379).

**101 stack suites (81): 90 `*.db.test.mjs`, 11 `*.integration.test.mjs`**, run by `pnpm test:db` (`.github/workflows/database.yml:106`) only when `DB_PATHS` matches. cats.name: Code Style / Static Analysis
cats.verdict: The ratchets hold, and the lint's own bank now takes only falls. The function limits are errors in 35 trees, unused names are errors, `@ts-ignore` is refused, and accessibility is linted under a baseline. The three gaps named on 28 Sep remain: no rule reads types, e2e is never typechecked (its errors went from 3 to 5), and the 55k-line shell sits outside the typecheck and Prettier. This is the top of a 7: the first two are S steps.
evidence: **Limits with teeth, in more trees:** complexity, max-lines-per-function and max-depth are errors in 35 `LIMITED_TREES` (29 on 28 Sep) and max-params in 23 (21) (`eslint.config.mjs:222-278`, `:444-457`). A ratchet holds 180 functions over the limit elsewhere (100 of them in the shell) and 13 files over 800 lines, all in the shell (`baselines/complexity.json`, `file-length.json`). `repo/lint-boundaries.test.mjs:356-525` proves ESLint applies the limits in each tree and counts as the ratchet does.

**The lint banks only falls** (#1257): `bankWarnings` (`tooling/scripts/checks/lint.mjs:59-70`) and the bundle's `bankBudget` write the lower count and never a new entry, and `--raise` is a separate command. `repo/measures.test.mjs:77-109` holds both. The 321 warnings in 62 files are 128 exhaustive-deps plus 193 a11y findings; 320 of them are in the shell (`baselines/lint-warnings.json`).

**New rules since 28 Sep:** unused names are errors in our TypeScript (`eslint.config.mjs:42-45`, test `lint-boundaries.test.mjs:510`, #1328 from #1230). The jsx-a11y recommended set runs over all dashboard markup, held by the baseline (`:72-77`, `:489-494`). `@ts-ignore` and `@ts-nocheck` are refused, and `@ts-expect-error` needs a reason (`:51-60`, #1304). `no-console` covers the dashboard server (`:343-351`, #1332), and a surface may not draw raw controls (`:168-202`). There are 0 `@ts-ignore` and 0 explicit `any` outside the type tests.

cats.name: Product-Level Architecture
cats.verdict: Lifecycle and permissions moved: an account's deletion now ends a workspace it empties (paused, plan ended, never resumed), and a partner's password alone opens no definer door but one. The commercial layer is where it was: one Stripe price, every quota a constant, no entitlements, credits, usage ledger, flag registry or product analytics, and Ask plus five drafting doors spend the platform's key for a paused or unbilled workspace.
evidence: **An emptied workspace ends:** `delete_my_account` pauses it, stamps `left_empty_at` and revokes its invitations (`supabase/migrations/00262_a_workspace_its_last_member_leaves_is_ended.sql:68-80`); `DELETE /me` asks the edge's `end` (`apps/dashboard/src/server/workspace/billing.ts:31-40`); billing never resumes it (`apps/edge/lib/billing/billing.ts:210-225`); held by `tests/auth/account-deletion-ends-plans.test.mjs` (2 pass, run here) and `billing-door.test.mjs:852-875` (#1330).

**Routes:** 202 declared with scope, role, rate and spend, 0 undeclared (`tooling/scripts/tests/route-policy.json`); 7 `spend: true`, now incl. `POST lead-searches/import` for a list of one's own (#1329).

**Permission model:** four roles in `ROLE_PERMS`; 00261 puts the second-factor clause on nine definer doors a partner's password could open (`00261_a_partner_s_seat_opens_no_door_without_the_second_factor.sql:13-22`, #1330); an existing workspace can bring in a partner (0020, 00225, #1206).
**Notifications:** 20 server kinds (`contracts/src/today/notifications.ts:209-233`), `reach_out_day` new for the 6 PM bell (#1325), delivered by bell, email, push and pager through `notifyOnce`.
**Subscription state is pure:** `maySpend` and `planBilling` (`contracts/src/workspace/billing.ts:145`, `:251`), the paused words shown to owners (`:248-249`).
gaps: **Entitlements and credits:** one `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` (`apps/edge/lib/billing/billing.ts:65`); every quota a constant equal on trial and plan: `ASK_TOKENS_DAY` (`contracts/src/ask/ask.ts:53`), `LEAD_MONTHLY_ALLOWANCE` (`leads/search/caps.ts:13`), `REACH_OUT_READS_PER_DAY` (`reach-out-replies.ts:68`), `REACH_OUT_CHECKS_PER_DAY` (`reach-out-rules.ts:64`). Decision 0010 says "decided, not built" (`docs/decisions/0010-leads-are-paid-per-verified-lead.md:3`); the pricing draft #1039 is conflicting.

**Model spend outside billing:** `POST ask`, `ask/warm`, `leads/[id]/draft`, `segments/draft`, `templates/draft`, `PUT lead-suggestions` and `google/reviews/[id]/draft` are `spend: false` (`route-policy.json`), the gateway reads no billing (`apps/edge/api/admin/llm.ts:46-89`), and the Google review sweep reads no status (`listing-check.ts:170-181`).
**Metering:** no usage ledger or dollars; usage rows purged at 30 days (`retention.ts:14,52-53`); the reply reader, the reach-out check and the notes sweep write no usage row (defect 53).

**Flags and analytics:** switches live in env (`apps/edge/lib/env.ts:57,71,83,166,175,183,186`) and `ASK_MODEL`, none audited or expiring; `page_vitals` is performance field data (00255), and nothing records activation, a funnel or retention.

**Lifecycle:** no door closes a workspace short of deleting one's account, and nothing erases an ended one: 00262 says the platform erases it later (`:14-15`), but no migration, sweep or script does (new defect).

steps.t: Build 0010 as a pure `entitlements(workspace)` that every gate reads, caps as a row per plan that SQL and pages share, and settle #1039 (tiers with extra usage vs credits).
Bring model spend into billing: `spend: true` on Ask and the drafting doors (or a billing read in the gateway), the review sweep skipping paused and ended workspaces, and a per-plan token cap.
A kept usage ledger with dollars and a monthly rollup for every model path, and a Usage page for owners.
One flag registry with per-workspace overrides and audit events; activation events and a funnel in the back office; a close-workspace door and an erase rule for ended workspaces.

defects.what: **A new field inside a settings section can silence the receptionist.** Sections are `.strict()` on read, so an older edge refuses the whole config when it meets a key it doesn't know. This happens after a dashboard-first deploy or an edge rollback, on the first save of the new field. `configBroken` then goes true, and every inbound message is held with no reply. #1005 shipped `ask_email` this way on 24 Sep.

defects.what: **A mailbox read that fails loses whatever reply the heartbeat was sending.** The tick builds the email wire for every job, and `emailWireFor` reads the workspace's mailbox with `mailboxOfTenant`, which throws on an error. The throw leaves dispatch, and an `outbound_send` is never retried, so a WhatsApp or SMS reply that needs no email is failed as “may have sent”, its thread flagged “A reply never left” and the owner alerted. Run end to end over the real tick route and the suite's fake database (review/F/probe-tick-blips.mjs case B: no Graph send, job failed `mailbox: connection reset`). The code predates 26 Sep and is not in the register; #1148 does not touch it.

The reach-out clock's `neverLeft` knows only a 429, never_delivered and orphaned, so it marks the send `send_failed`, and that lead's step is lost for the run although nothing left. The next sign-in in that tab hydrates those rows at module scope, before React and before the tenant guard, which runs only after the whole boot. The mechanism is proved on the real module (`review/G/signout-cache-probe.mjs`); the end-to-end timing is not. On the web the window is short, and the app replaces its WebViews on sign-out.

**Fourteen edge doors answer a JSON `null` body with a crash, one of them before it checks who is knocking.** #1254 made `readBody` turn a non-object into `{}`, but only the 4 doors that use it got the fix. The 14 doors that `JSON.parse` by hand into `let body = {}` keep `null` and then read `body.x`, which throws a TypeError. The platform answers that with an unhandled 500 where validation would give a 400. `sending-domains` reads `body.op` before `authorizeAdmin`, so an anonymous `POST` with the body `null` crashes the function. Probe `review3/C/probe-null-body2.mjs`: sending-domains throws with no credentials; stop-call, hand-over and steer throw with a key. No data is touched.

defects.what: **The edge's closed code set stops at the edge.** `EdgeAnswer.body` is `Record<string, unknown>`, so the dashboard compares edge codes as plain strings at 11 sites, and only `connections/sending-domains.ts` writes `satisfies EdgeErrorCode`. The dashboard also mints four codes no set names (`edge_timeout`, `edge_unreachable`, `preview`, `no_edge_credential`). If the edge renames `no_line_provider` or `campaign_rejected`, both typechecks and the error-codes test pass, and the owner silently gets the generic 502 words instead of the specific ones. Latent: every compared code is in the set today (`review3/C/edge-codes-read.mjs`).

**A member can attach a message to another workspace's thread or person, and the service code acts on the pair.** The member insert policy checks the row's own `tenant_id` but not that `conversation_id` or `contact_id` belong to it, and foreign-key checks ignore RLS. A member of workspace B who knows one of workspace A's conversation or contact ids (a former employee of A, say) can queue such a row through PostgREST. Two services then act on it:
- After 10 minutes the edge's orphan sweep reads every queued row with no tenant filter, marks it failed and writes an escalation for (B, A's conversation). `escalations_one_open` is unique on `conversation_id` alone, so B's row takes the thread's one open slot. From then on A's own `upsertEscalation` hits 23505, its tenant-filtered update matches nothing, and it returns `refreshed`: A's handovers on that thread never show in A's Inbox.
- 00259's moments trigger joins `contacts` on the message's `contact_id` without the tenant. B's row (any `created_at`, `meta.backfill`, and a status B may move to `delivered` through its column grant) rewrites A's person's first and last moments, which order People and decide who is new.
Traced through the code; not run on a stack. The 28 Sep gap named the missing clause; the harm and the 00259 path are new.
defects.note: The policy hole is read by the lead; the downstream effects on the other workspace's escalations are traced, not run.

defects.what: **An emptied workspace's plan is ended by one call that nothing retries.** `DELETE /me` asks the edge's billing `end` once, after the account is already gone. A failure (edge unreachable, Stripe refusing, or a timeout) is only logged (`account_delete_plan_not_ended`), and the test accepts it. No billing reconcile cron exists, and `trial_will_end` only records the date. The plan is therefore canceled only by its next subscription event, which for a live or trialing plan is the renewal that has already charged the card.

**Any signed-in person can ask two lead-finder helpers about any workspace.** `lead_month(p_tenant_id)` and `lead_searches_on(p_tenant_id)` are SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`, and check no membership. Given a workspace id, a stranger learns its current month in its own time zone and whether it may search. The leak is small, but they are the only session-callable definers besides `platform_*` (which check admin) that name a tenant and never ask who is calling.

**A broadcast burns its list when Graph cannot be reached.** Wave 2 says a connection that never opened is `retryable`: the send provably did not leave (`provider-fetch.ts:104-112,130`). The broadcast gives a person back only for Graph's throttle (`graphThrottled`, via `namedFailure`). Any other failure is marked `failed/send_failed` and the batch goes on. Sends are `breaker: "count"`, so the breaker never holds them. Probe (real `sendText`, real core `deliver`, real `sendBroadcastBatch`, fetch refusing every connection): 4 people, 4 calls, all 4 marked `failed/send_failed`. The run then finishes and tells the owner “Broadcast sent”. A DNS or network blip during a run burns every recipient it reaches.
defects.note: Re-run by the lead: 4 of 4 recipients `failed/send_failed`, the finish alert “Broadcast “Offer” sent”.

defects.what: **A stalled broadcast waits without bound and can resume outside sending hours.** #1326 made a batch whose credentials cannot be read reschedule itself a minute on, with nobody claimed; a batch whose people cannot be read already did. Neither wait is counted or bounded, and neither checks the business's hours. Only the throttle back-off asks `nextOpenMoment` (`broadcast.ts:405`), and `scheduleNext` schedules at the time given (`packages/jobs/src/broadcast-send.ts:207-209`). A vault outage from 7:50 PM to 11 PM re-queues the run about 190 times, then sends the day's template at 11 PM. The file itself says it must never do that (`broadcast.ts:391-394`). Traced, not run.

**The provider breaker is two breakers.** Core's build inlines `@chanlytics/channels`, so each instance has its own breaker map in `packages/channels/dist/index.js:6` and another in `packages/core/dist/index.js:978`. Sends made through core's `deliver`/`whatsappSender` count toward a breaker the edge's direct calls (template sync, media, Retell reads through channels) never consult, and the reverse. `breakerOf` reports only one of them. An outage is learned more slowly than the header's 'one per provider in this instance' promises.

**The 6 PM reach-out line reads the zone without `safe_zone`.** `reach_out_day_due` (00241, #1325) reads `tenants.timezone` raw, platform-wide, the pattern 00245 replaced for the sweeps. A name Postgres cannot read would raise and stop every workspace's line. An offset such as '+05:00', which the save's Intl check accepts (Node 22 accepts '+05:00' and '-0300'; measured), is read by Postgres with its sign flipped (00245's own header), so that workspace's line fires hours off. Not run on Postgres.

**A provider's breaker opens and holds calls in silence.** After five faults the breaker holds that provider's non-send calls for 30 s, answering `retryable`/`breaker_open`, but nothing logs the opening, no caller names `breaker_open`, and `breakerOf` is read by no code (not /api/diag, not /api/health). During a Meta or Twilio outage the only trace is each caller's own failure words (“google: breaker_open”).

**The texting line's token refresh calls any failure a refusal of the platform's credentials.** `refreshLineToken` answers every non-`ok` outcome, a Twilio 503, a 429 or a timeout included, as `provider_unauthorized` with “the provider refused the platform's credentials”, logs `line_token_refresh_refused`, and the A2P sync writes that on the line's `last_error`, sending an operator to the master key during a Twilio blip. Traced, not run; the words predate #1332, which gave them the code.

**Closing Ask while it listens asks whatever it had heard.** Closing calls `speech.stop()`, which stops the recogniser (the microphone is not left on), but its `onend` then hands the words heard so far to `onHeard`, so a half-spoken question is submitted after the window has closed.

**Import leads reads and parses a chosen file whole, on the main thread, before its 500-row cap applies, and a failed read is silent.** `onFile` calls `readAsText` on any file with no size check and no `onerror`, then `leadImportPlanOf` parses every line before `tooMany` compares the ready rows with `LEAD_LIST_MAX` (500), and the sheet re-filters every parsed row on each render. A large export (tens of MB) freezes the tab; an unreadable one leaves the sheet as it was with no word.

**The bundle budget banks un-argued growth on every raise.** A build within 1% of the budget passes, and `--raise` writes the sums as measured, so growth that crept in under the band rides into the next argued raise. The register shows it: after #1210 set 962.0 KB, main measured 970.1 KB before #1206 argued 2.3 KB and banked 972.4; main then measured 976.1 before #1325 argued 6.3 and banked 982.4. About 12 of the 21 KB regained since #1210 was argued by nobody. A fall inside the band is never banked either.

**A paused or ended workspace keeps answering Google reviews in public.** The hourly sweep picks every connection by its sync time alone and `answerNewReviews` asks only the reviews mode, so a workspace whose plan stopped, or one 00262 ended because its last member deleted their account, keeps drafting on the platform's key and posting replies under the business's name, while the owner is told only that messages wait and 00262 promises the receptionist stops. Needs the reviews class set to auto (the default is ask).
defects.note: Re-read by the lead: `connectionsDue` selects by sync age alone and `answerNewReviews` checks only the reviews mode.

defects.what: **An ended workspace is kept for ever.** 00262 says a workspace its last member leaves is kept "for the platform to erase … later", and the privacy words say everything else stays while the workspace exists; no migration, sweep, script or door erases a workspace (grep for `erase_tenant`, `erase_workspace`, `purge_tenant`, `left_empty_at` finds only 00262 and billing), so its customers' threads, calls and numbers stay with nobody able to reach them.

**The 0017 reply draft skips the receptionist's layer 2.** `replyDrafter` hands back the brain's text as it came: no `layerTwo`, no `violatesNoPrices`, no price warning like the Ask reply card's, so a price the model wrote sits in a draft a person may send as written.

**The nightly fails every night on a role list written before partners.** `roles are the widened set and nothing kept 'staff'` asserts every membership is owner, operator or viewer. 00201 made partner a fourth role, and the nightly's database holds a partner membership, so the test fails there every run ("unexpected role partner", run 36458417242). The local stack's seed has no partner, so `database.yml`'s replay passes it and no pull request gate sees it.

**Two cron door tests pass only when no database is configured.** `refusedAtTheDoor` ends with `setPg(null)` and expects `no_database`, but `pg()` builds a real client whenever `SUPABASE_URL` and the service key are set. Five door tests delete those variables first; the two reach-out doors do not. So both fail in the nightly, which sets them for `pnpm test`, and in any shell with a `.env` loaded (2 of the nightly's 3 node failures on 28 Sep).

**Since the TypeScript catalog, Dependabot drops the root's dev tools.** The npm update job succeeded on 7197be0aa and failed on both runs since b28d3791d (36494688993, 36518966053). Its pnpm 11.25 answers `Invalid Version: ^3.9.9` (and `^4.23.15`, `^8.70.1`) for prettier, tsx and typescript-eslint, the root package.json's dev dependencies. Those three left the weekly group (15 updates on 28 Sep, 12 in #1315) and get no PR at all, while the run still reports partial success. The cause is likely `catalogMode: strict`; it is inferred from the timing, not reproduced.

**A bump of channels' html-to-text can never pass CI.** Core and jobs bundle channels (`noExternal: [/^@chanlytics\//]`) without declaring its dependencies, so tsup inlines html-to-text, htmlparser2 and entities into their committed dist (9 and 11 module markers; channels itself imports html-to-text). Dependabot's #767 changes only the manifest and lockfile, so the dist-drift guard fails it on the rewritten core and jobs bundles. It has been red since 21 Sep, and the same third-party code ships in three bundles.

**The title rule holds the PR title, not the subject that lands on main.** `pr-title.mjs` checks `github.event.pull_request.title` on open, synchronize and reopen. The squash subject is whatever the merger types: #1329's title is 92 characters, but it landed as a 122-character subject. Ten squash subjects since 28 Sep (#1279, #1286, #1293, #1298, #1301 to #1304, #1310, #1311) drop the `(#N)` the rest of history carries, so `git log` loses the link from those commits to their PRs.

**The nightly's Ask day check reads any failure as 'Ask crossed a line'.** The step runs with `continue-on-error`, and the next step opens an issue titled "Ask's cache or first words crossed a line" whenever its outcome is failure. `ask-day.mjs` also exits 2 when its variables are missing, and exits non-zero on any thrown read. The body is `tail -n 1` of stdout, so a crash files an alarm about Ask's cache with an empty or unrelated line. It has not run yet: the last nightly (f2a9752fd) predates #1319.

**Folded and superseded lanes leave their branches on the remote.** 21 of 31 non-main branches have no open PR. Among them are `fix/the-sweeps-read-only-what-is-due`, `fix/a-retell-outage-is-not-a-failed-recording` and `fix/a-credentials-blip-is-not-a-disconnect`, whose work landed as cherry-picks in #1323, #1322 and #1326, and four `scale/*` branches folded into #1328. `delete_branch_on_merge` deletes only a merged PR's own head, so each fold or supersede leaves a branch, and the next session can mistake it for open work.
defects.where: repository branches (gh api, 29 Sep); repository setting `delete_branch_on_merge: true`
